trustCenter.repositoryDescription:
Paramify-hosted Trust Center publishing our FedRAMP compliance
posture, control implementation status. Documentation is available to
approved visitors upon request.
trustCenter.accessRequestInstructions:
Go to Request Access -> Fill in the required information under Trust Center
Access Request -> Submit forapproval
trustCenter.agencyAccessDenialProcess:
Vbrick will notify FedRAMP within five (5) business days of denying an
agency's request for access to FedRAMP Certification Data, using the
required notification form (CSPs Agency Access Denial), available at:
https://help.fedramp.gov/hc/en-us/requests/new?ticket_form_id=518298266
17243

secureConfigurationGuidance.repositoryDescription:

informationResources.metadataIncludedInScope:
Yes. Metadata about federal customer data - including authentication data,
customer metadata, PII, and system-generated analytics - is included in
scope, stored across MongoDB, Elasticsearch and AWS S3.

resources.name: Vbrick Rev (EVP) Application Servers (EC2)
resources.descriptionAndRole:
EC2 instances running the core video platform application —
handles upload, transcoding

resources.name: AWS S3
resources.descriptionAndRole: AWS S3 buckets storing customer-uploaded data

resources.name: MongoDB
resources.descriptionAndRole:
MongoDB stores authentication data, customer metadata,
personally identifiable information (PII)

resources.name: Elasticsearch
resources.descriptionAndRole:
Stores customer metadata, supplemental metadata, and
system-generated analytics.

certifiedServices.serviceDescription:
Rev enables organizations to securely and efficiently deliver high
quality live and on-demand video to huge audiences internally,
using the organizations wide area network, and externally via the
cloud. Features of Rev include, the central management of video
assets, user access and permissions, network delivery devices,
and video publishing and distribution - in the most bandwidth-
efficient way possible.

informationFlows.dataFlowDiagramReference:
EVP Cloud Service Data Flow Diagram, APPENDIX G -
Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP)

flows.informationTypeCarried:
Login credentials (username/password); LDAP
authentication requests/responses; SSO authentication
data, session cookies/authentication tokens
flows.explanation:
Viewers authenticate via local credentials, LDAP (customer directory), or
SSO (customer provider). A session cookie with authentication token is
issued on success, valid for a tenant-configurable period (default 30 min).

flows.destinationResource:
EVP Application Servers (cid:0) Customer Content Storage
(AWS S3)
flows.informationTypeCarried:
Video content, metadata and temporary workflow data
removed upon completion
flows.explanation:
Authenticated user uploads video via the UI over HTTPS.
Stored in a tenant-specific, encrypted S3 bucket; optionally
transcoded (tenant-configurable) with output stored in the
same directory. User sets permissions before the video
becomes viewable.

flows.destinationResource:
EVP Application Servers (cid:0) Customer Content Storage
(AWS S3)
flows.explanation:
Device is configured with an access key pair and uploads
video via HTTPS. Storage/transcoding follow the same
process as direct upload. Video is not activated by default (cid:0)
typically requires manual admin action, per tenant policy.

flows.sourceResource: Third-party software or integrated service (via API)
flows.destinationResource:
EVP Application Servers (cid:0) Customer Content Storage
(AWS S3)
flows.explanation:
Integrated service authenticated with an assigned API key
pair and video is uploaded via HTTPS. Storage/transcoding
follow the same process as direct upload. Video is not
activated by default (cid:0) typically requires manual admin
action, per tenant policy.

certified.useCase:
AWS infrastructure supporting application hosting, storage, containers, and
networking.
certified.usageAndConfiguration: Resources are deployed across AWS US East-West regions.
certified.justificationForUse:
Required to support application workloads and computing
requirements.
certified.mitigationMeasures:
Encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access, network
segmentation.
certified.compensatingControls:
Vulnerability scanning is performed on Vbrick-managed workloads hosted
within AWS and network configuration reviewed periodically.

nonCertified.name:
CrowdStrike Falcon (Exposure Management / Cloud
Security Posture Management)
nonCertified.useCase:
Cloud security services - Vulnerability Management, Cloud Security Posture
Management
nonCertified.usageAndConfiguration: Deployed through sensor installation and by AWS integration
nonCertified.justificationForUse:
Used to support vulnerability identification, cloud security
posture assessment, and container image scanning.
nonCertified.mitigationMeasures:
Access is limited to the information and environments required to perform
the defined security functions. Tool does not access or store federal
customer data.
nonCertified.compensatingControls:
Scan findings are reviewed internally through the Information Security
Program, access to the Falcon console is restricted to authorized personnel
only.

policiesAndProcedures.name: Certification Data Sharing Policy
policiesAndProcedures.summary:
Defines requirements for sharing applicable FedRAMP
certification data publicly, including use of a
FedRAMP-compatible trust center.

policiesAndProcedures.name: Certification Data Sharing Procedure
policiesAndProcedures.summary:
Defines the operational steps for implementing the
Certification Data Sharing Policy, including trust center
maintenance and agency access management.
